edition.witness_note: Lake 1912 Loeb copy-text; Lightfoot/Funk middle recension not yet locked as second witness

source_text: [1] Εἰ γὰρ καὶ κατὰ σάρκα μέ τινες ἠθέλησαν πλανῆσαι, ἀλλὰ τὸ πνεῦμα οὐ πλανᾶται ἀπὸ θεοῦ ὄν. οἶδεν γάρ, πόθεν ἔρχεται καὶ ποῦ ὑπάγει, καὶ τὰ κρυπτὰ ἐλέγχει. ἐκραύγασα μεταξὺ ὤν, ἐλάλουν μεγάλῃ φωνῇ, θεοῦ φωνῇ: Τῷ ἐπισκοπῳ προσέχετε καὶ τῷ πρεσβυτερίῳ καὶ διακόνοις. [2] οἱ δὲ ὑποπτεύσαντές με ὡς προειδότα τὸν μερισμόν τινων λέγειν ταῦτα: μάρτυς δέ μοι, ἐν ᾧ δέδεμαι, ὅτι ἀπὸ σαρκὸς ἀνθρωπίνης οὐκ ἔγνων. τὸ δὲ πνεῦμα ἐκήρυσσεν λέγον τάδε: Χωρὶς τοῦ ἐπισκόπου μηδὲν ποιεῖτε, τὴν σάρκα ὑμῶν ὡς ναὸν θεοῦ τηρεῖτε, τὴν ἕνωσιν ἀγαπᾶτε, τοὺς μερισμοὺς φεύγετε, μιμηταὶ γίνεσθε Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὡς καὶ αὐτὸς τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ.
pass_a_gloss: For even if some wished to deceive me according to the flesh, yet the Spirit is not deceived, being from God. For it knows where it comes from and where it goes (John 3:8), and it exposes the hidden things. I cried out when I was among you; I was speaking with a loud voice, with God's voice: Pay attention to the bishop and to the presbytery and deacons. But some suspected me of saying these things because I knew in advance about the division of certain people. But he in whom I am bound is my witness that I did not learn it from human flesh. The Spirit was proclaiming, saying this: Do nothing without the bishop; keep your flesh as a temple of God; love unity; flee divisions; become imitators of Jesus Christ, as he also is of his Father.
pass_b_english: For even if some wished to deceive me according to the flesh, the Spirit is not deceived, for it is from God. It knows where it comes from and where it is going (John 3:8), and it lays bare what is hidden. While I was with you I cried out; I spoke with a loud voice, God's own voice: "Pay attention to the bishop, to the presbytery, and to the deacons."

Some suspected that I said this because I already knew of the split among certain people. But the One in whom I am bound is my witness that I did not learn it from human flesh. The Spirit was preaching, saying this: "Do nothing without the bishop. Guard your flesh as God's temple. Love unity. Run from divisions. Become imitators of Jesus Christ, as he is of his Father (1 Corinthians 11:1)."

choices.why: Capitalized: the Spirit who speaks through him and 'proclaims' in 7.2. The neuter pronoun 'it' follows the Greek and John 3:8.
Ignatius claims prophetic speech; kept short and strong.

choices.english: I did not learn it from human flesh
choices.why: Keeps σάρξ so the flesh/Spirit contrast stands.
rejected: I got no intelligence from any man

choices.english: Do nothing ... Guard ... Love ... Run ... Become
choices.why: The Spirit's message is a string of commands; kept as separate short sentences.
rejected: one long list joined by semicolons

anf_compare.notes: Same sense. ANF 'for whose sake I am in bonds' loosens ἐν ᾧ δέδεμαι (in whom I am bound); ANF 'bodies' for σάρκα.

bible_refs.note: μιμηταί μου γίνεσθε καθὼς κἀγὼ Χριστοῦ; same form of the imitation command

notes: 'Keep your flesh as God's temple' may echo 1 Corinthians 3:16-17 or 6:19; not cited inline.
'Lays bare what is hidden' may echo 1 Corinthians 14:24-25; not cited inline.
Whether τὸ πνεῦμα is the Holy Spirit or Ignatius's own spirit is debated; the prophetic frame favors the Holy Spirit.
Source shows 'ἐπισκοπῳ' without accent; reproduced as supplied.

checker_dispute: checker b says Pass A lacks the John 3:8 citation. Inline Scripture belongs in Pass B, where it stands beside 'οἶδεν γάρ, πόθεν ἔρχεται καὶ ποῦ ὑπάγει' (John 3:8: 'οὐκ οἶδας πόθεν ἔρχεται καὶ ποῦ ὑπάγει').

checker_dispute: checker b prefers 1 Corinthians 4:16. 1 Corinthians 4:16 has only 'μιμηταί μου γίνεσθε'; 1 Corinthians 11:1 adds the matching second limb 'καθὼς κἀγὼ Χριστοῦ', which is the shape of 'μιμηταὶ γίνεσθε Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὡς καὶ αὐτὸς τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ'. Kept 1 Corinthians 11:1.
checker_dispute: inline Scripture is house rule; John 3:8 now also marked in Pass A beside οἶδεν γάρ, πόθεν ἔρχεται καὶ ποῦ ὑπάγει.

review.notes: Paragraph [1] checked clause by clause. Greek 'Εἰ γὰρ καὶ κατὰ σάρκα μέ τινες ἠθέλησαν πλανῆσαι, ἀλλὰ τὸ πνεῦμα οὐ πλανᾶται ἀπὸ θεοῦ ὄν' matches Pass A 'For even if some wished to deceive me according to the flesh, yet the Spirit is not deceived, being from God' and Pass B 'For even if some wished to deceive me according to the flesh, the Spirit is not deceived, for it is from God.' Negation holds in 'οὐκ ἔγνων' / 'I did not learn it from human flesh' and 'μηδὲν ποιεῖτε' / 'Do nothing without the bishop.' Agency holds: 'ἐκραύγασα' is 'I cried out'; 'τὸ δὲ πνεῦμα ἐκήρυσσεν' is 'The Spirit was proclaiming/preaching.' 'πόθεν ἔρχεται καὶ ποῦ ὑπάγει' is cited (John 3:8) in both passes beside 'where it comes from and where it goes.' Commands through 'μιμηταὶ γίνεσθε Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὡς καὶ αὐτὸς τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ' are kept. Title names the prophetic cry, not only the locus.

Source identity confirmed: Ignatius Philadelphians 7 matches supplied Greek. Completeness: all clauses from both paragraphs covered, no omissions. Negation: 'οὐ πλανᾶται' rendered 'is not deceived', 'οὐκ ἔγνων' rendered 'did not learn'. Agency: Spirit as subject of knows/exposes/proclaims; Ignatius as subject of cried out/spoke; 'he in whom I am bound' as witness. Modality: indicative mood preserved. Doctrine: flesh/Spirit contrast maintained, unity/anti-division emphasis, imitation of Christ. Scripture: John 3:8 correctly cited beside 'ποθεν ἔρχεται καὶ που ὑπάγει' in both Pass A and B; 1 Corinthians 11:1 correctly cited beside imitation clause in Pass B. Title 'The Spirit Cried Out' names the prophetic act, not just locus. Notes disclose OCR accent omission and interpretive disputes. Pass A and B mutually consistent, neither adds nor contradicts Greek.
